target_customer: Software developers who work in the command line, paying for team and pro features
problem: Terminals are hard for beginners and slow for experts because commands, flags and arguments must be remembered.
business_model: Freemium developer tool with paid team subscriptions

technical_complexity.rationale: Overlaying UI on many terminals required macOS accessibility hooks and a completion spec for hundreds of CLI tools.

defensibility.rationale: The open source completion specs were community built and copyable, but the integration across terminals took effort.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AWS acquired Fig in August 2023 and folded the technology into CodeWhisperer and later Amazon Q.

market_need_then: Developers lived in the terminal and a 2020 Product Hunt launch drew strong early interest; completion tools like zsh plugins existed but gave limited descriptions.

identity.logo: Fig logo, not described in sources found

rebrands.why: Standalone Fig was sunset and merged into AWS tooling; date from secondary sources.

branding.community_and_virality: A Discord server and an open source autocomplete repository with over 200 contributors, per mirrors of the project README.

brand_strength.rationale: Short memorable name and an active open source community; confusable with Figma in search. No mascot or merch found.

pivots.from: Visual apps and shortcuts for the terminal
pivots.to: Terminal autocomplete as the lead product
pivots.why: Autocomplete became the first product in the roadmap; the YC tagline lists apps, shortcuts and autocomplete.

outcome_analysis: Fig reached developers through free product led growth and a 2.2 million dollar seed in 2020, then was acquired by AWS in August 2023 as Amazon pushed generative AI coding tools. Standalone Fig was later sunset and folded into Amazon Q. The Series A mentioned in a 2022 interview is not confirmed. The exit looks like a talent and technology deal, with price undisclosed.
notes: fig.io fetch returned HTTP 503. Seed date of 2020-09 is approximate: TechCrunch describes the round as raised by an S20 company, with the exact month not seen. Competitor search surfaced no dated 2020 competitor coverage, so the list is empty. Sunset date varies by source (Sept 2024 vs Feb 2025), unverified. Series A not confirmed.
